title: Conan and Heiji's Nue Legend
notes: Case spans episodes 872-874 but only 0872 and 0874 subtitle files are available locally (0873 is missing from subs_resolved/); the Someji murder and immediate cave-in/nue backstory come from 0872, the full Tanzawa poisoning + Masuko Fumie reveal comes from 0874, so the middle episode's material (any additional interrogation scenes) is not represented here. Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan Edogawa, Ran Mouri) omitted by convention, matching ep011; Heiji Hattori and Kazuha Toyama are kept in because Heiji is the one who solves the case on-screen and Kazuha's fright/near-miss with a room swap is load-bearing to the plot. The Vermouth/Amuro-san cold-open gag at the very start of 0872 is an unrelated running subplot and is not part of this case's graph, consistent with the old file's own scoping note. Old cases/ file's stated culprit (Fumie Masuko, s3) is CORRECT per the transcript -- she confesses outright. However the old file was otherwise low-fidelity and had real errors: (1) it listed 'Michiki Tanzawa' as both a suspect (s2) and a separate victim (v2), duplicating one person into two nodes; (2) it listed Densuke Takekuma and Hajime Tsurumi as 'suspects' with no motive given, when the transcript gives them no criminal involvement at all (Tsurumi is a bystander invited as an unwitting witness, Densuke is the mayor who organized the treasure-hunt trip); (3) it omitted the entire real motive -- Masuko's late husband Charles Abel, a foreign archaeologist on the expedition 16 years earlier, was left to die in a cave-in by Someji and Tanzawa, and his misheard dying note ('tetsu'/metal, not 'nue') is the whole engine of the plot -- none of this appears in the old file. Conan's on-screen theory that documentary writer Hajime Tsurumi is actually Masuko and Charles's son is left as an open/unconfirmed relationship below: Masuko explicitly denies it in the transcript ('You idiot. Of course not.'), so it is recorded as disputed rather than asserted as fact. Per the current build rules, order/temporal_frame/years_before_present are omitted entirely from edges.

clues.desc: 16-year-old excavation photo: the foreigner in the middle (Charles Abel) closely resembles Hajime Tsurumi -- hints at an undisclosed family tie.

Charles Abel's recovered practice notebook has a torn page that exactly matches the torn edge of his old dying note, proving both came from him and that the note really read 'tetsu' (metal), not 'nue'.

The dog barked at the nue cry cue (wanting to fetch the decoy sign) but stayed silent when the 'giant monster' itself supposedly appeared -- proves the cry and the monster sighting were separately staged effects, not one real creature.
